answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and their read replicas, object storage (Amazon S3) used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer: engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled before it is issued and at all times afterward. IT maintains an inventory of all Tidewell-issued laptops, including assigned user, model, serial number, and security status. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically, and if not fixed within 3 days they lose access to corporate systems until compliant again.

answers.answer: Our documents do not say whether the full penetration test report can be shared under NDA. What we do make available is a Penetration Test Summary Letter, which customers can get on request. It comes from the independent tester, Brightline Security, and covers the 2026 annual test.

**Re:** 2026 Annual Penetration Test — Summary of Results
Brightline Security, LLC ("Brightline") was engaged by Tidewell Data, Inc. ("Tidewell") to perform an independent penetration test of the Tidewell platform.

answers.reasoning_note: The KB-01 Trust Center and KB-17 only cover the summary letter (on request). Nothing says whether the full report is shared under NDA (only the SOC 2 report is listed as under NDA), so a human must decide. The KB-32 2024 answer library is outdated and wasn't used.

No passage says whether a 24/7 SOC exists or what hours are covered. Related: KB-06 §7 (automated detection rules, alerts to Security team queue, escalation per IRP) and KB-10 §6.2 (SEV1 triage within 30 minutes).

answers.answer: Under the current Information Security Policy (v3.2, effective February 1, 2026), the Head of Security owns the security program day to day and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly. The Chief Technology Officer is the accountable executive for the information security program. A Security & Compliance team implements and monitors security controls. Our documents do not name the individual in this role or give the size of the security team.

citations.passage: **Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day. Maintains this policy and its supporting standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly.
**Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: No retrieved source mentions a CISO title, names the security leader, or gives team headcount, so a human must supply those. KB-32 (2024) and superseded KB-03 v2.4 say the Director of Engineering owns the program; that is outdated, and current KB-02 v3.2 names the Head of Security.
